title: Orchestration
lede: How one orchestrator turns owner requests into merged work by handing tasks to subagents in their own lanes.

request.name: Owner requests
request.role: Only the owner creates tasks; the agent records the request in the queue.
details: The agent runs queue add --requested with the owner's words and an acceptance check.

more: queue.db holds typed tasks: status, owner, accept, evidence.
queue.md is the committed view; line order is priority.
Every worktree reads the same record.

risks: An agent never adds its own tasks; its findings go to the owner instead.

dispatch.name: Dispatch
dispatch.role: On each loop tick, the orchestrator gives the top suited task to a free worker slot.
details: It reads the slots from topology.json.
It creates the worktree lane first, off the working branch's HEAD, then claims the task for that slot.

more: The orchestrator adds ORCH UPDATE notes to the task.
The subagent follows the newest one at its next checkpoint.

work.name: Subagent works
work.role: The subagent builds its one task in its own worktree and commits locally.
details: It starts with an ff-only check that it is on the working branch's HEAD.
A chore is built directly; a feature runs design, PRD, plan, TDD and refine; an interactive feature chain adds QA.
It validates, commits, records evidence and never pushes.
risks: A subagent that skips its checkpoints misses the orchestrator's steering.

integrate.name: Integrate
integrate.role: The orchestrator merges the target into the lane, re-runs the gates and merges green work into the one working branch.
details: Red gates block the merge; a subagent finishes the branch.
Then it opens a PR with Critical changes and verifies the real checks on the final head.
risks: There is exactly one working branch per session; two long-lived branches split the work.

ship.name: Authorized merge
ship.role: With the owner's session or standing authorization, the orchestrator squash-merges and queue advance records the delivery.
details: The PR lands on main as one squash commit.
queue advance --pr --branch records the merge and the fresh branch.
qs: Why can't the orchestrator merge to main on its own?

worktree.d: An isolated git checkout per worker, so workers never collide.

slot.d: A worker seat (a model plus a tool) that the orchestrator hands tasks to; its id names the task owner.

ffonly.d: Fast-forward only: the worker proves it starts from the working branch's HEAD, or stops.

orchupdate.d: The orchestrator's steering note on a running worker's task.

ask.context: The reader wants to understand how scaffold's orchestrator splits work across subagents and lands it on main.
